competency_fulfillment.rationale: The explain items are sound, and asking why a ruler's edge counts as a straight line does draw out a reason. The identify items undercut themselves: a stem stating that a ball has a surface that bends smoothly in every direction, or that a box has six faces that are each flat, hands over the defining property verbatim, so the learner matches keywords instead of recognising the attribute.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Four categories are named in the competency and all four are asked about, but the three-dimensional side rests on exactly two solids, one all-flat and one all-curved. The case a Grade 2 lesson turns on, a single object carrying both a flat and a curved surface, never appears, so surfaces are never contrasted within one object.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Explanations are phrased in the plainest available terms, bending and not bending, with no formal geometric vocabulary imported. The winding river and plate rim examples are drawn from ordinary experience, which is the right register for describing lines and surfaces at the end of Grade 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the nine seeds is a four-option selection, and not one presents an actual figure or solid to inspect. For a competency about what things look like and feel like, an entirely verbal treatment is a real omission; there is also no sorting or matching orientation across the four categories.

competency_alignment.rationale: The axis that moves between seeds is which of the four named categories is in play and whether the item asks for identification or for a stated difference. Both are dimensions of this competency rather than imported ones, and the contrast items directly target the difference the wording asks learners to explain.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency carries no numeric ceiling, and the only quantity that surfaces anywhere is the count of a box's faces. That is consistent with the descriptive, non-computational nature of the objective.
